evidence.finding: Adherence declined at incident onset from 91.8% at 09:00 to 73.5% at 09:15, then progressively fell to 55.1% by 11:45.
Productive agents fell from 45 at 09:00 to 36 at 09:15 and reached 27 by 11:45, below the forecast requirement of 36-40 agents throughout most of the incident.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49 agents, with zero agents in training, isolating the capacity loss to adherence/productive availability.
Service level fell from 93.0% at 09:00 to 50.6% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target through 11:45, reaching a low of 25.5% at 10:30.
ASA rose from 23.2 seconds at 09:00 to 80.2 seconds at 09:15 and peaked at 111.7 seconds at 10:30.
Abandonments increased from zero at 09:00 to 22 at 09:15 and peaked at 41 at 10:30 as productive capacity remained below requirement.

Demand was moderately above forecast during several early incident intervals, including 93 versus 79 calls at 09:15 and 100 versus 78 at 10:30, but was near or below forecast in other intervals and declined late in the window.
Queue outcomes varied by interval, but degradation affected multiple queues rather than remaining isolated to one destination; at 10:30 all four queues had service levels between 8.7% and 34.2%.
No routing-change or platform-incident events were supplied for the evaluation window.

primary_root_cause_detail: Beginning at 09:15, adherence fell from 91.8% to 73.5% and continued declining to 55.1%, while productive staffing dropped from 45 to 36 and ultimately 27 agents. All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in, so the capacity loss was caused by logged-in agents becoming nonproductive rather than absenteeism or insufficient scheduled headcount. The data do not identify why adherence declined.
recommended_actions: Immediately investigate the agent-state and exception records beginning at 09:15 to identify why logged-in agents became nonproductive.
Establish real-time adherence alerts and escalation thresholds tied to productive staffing versus forecast-required agents.
Restore productive capacity through supervisor intervention, schedule recovery, approved overtime, or cross-skilled backup when adherence creates a forecast staffing deficit.
Review intraday demand at 09:15 and 10:30 and maintain contingency capacity for moderate above-forecast volume.
Monitor recovery using productive-agent count, occupancy, ASA, abandonment rate, and queue-level service level.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Actual demand was only moderately and intermittently above forecast, while service degradation persisted even as offered volume moved near or below forecast. The much larger, sustained productive-staffing loss aligns more directly with the incident.
Scheduled and logged-in headcount remained stable at 49; the effective shortage arose from falling adherence and productive staffing, making ADHERENCE_DROP the deeper supported cause.
Actual AHT remained broadly aligned with forecast and did not rise at incident onset; it was 380.3 seconds at 09:15 versus a 374.3-second forecast and later often fell below forecast.
No routing event was recorded, transfer rates remained near 6%, queue totals reconcile with aggregate traffic, and degradation was not confined to one queue.
Queue staffing remained fixed and multiple queues experienced degradation. The broader center-wide loss of productive agents provides stronger causal evidence than a localized allocation imbalance.
Agents in training remained zero throughout the window.
No platform event was supplied, and calls continued to be answered with stable AHT and transfer rates.
Demand variance was mixed and modest across the full incident period; forecast error cannot explain the sharp decline from 45 to 27 productive agents.
Aggregate offered calls equal answered plus abandoned calls, and reported service levels agree with the supplied formula, so the incident is supported by internally consistent metrics.

stakeholder_summary: CC-007 was caused by a sustained adherence collapse, not a loss of logged-in headcount. Productive staffing dropped below forecast requirement at 09:15 and continued falling, creating a capacity deficit, rising waits and abandonments, and service levels as low as 25.5%. Moderate above-forecast volume amplified the impact at several intervals but was not the primary cause.
